newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African rand nears record low against dollar.
newsitem.headline: S.African rand nears record low against dollar.

text.p: The South Africa rand fell to within a whisker of its all-time low against the dollar in early trade on Thursday, hitting a two-month low of 4.5865 against the U.S. currency.

Foreign exchange dealers said the rand, which has slumped from 3.65 since last February, fell back in line with a weaker bond market that was hit by disappointing September inflation data out on Wednesday.
"Local banks rushed in to buy dollars this morning after bond (yields) shot up late yesterday," a rand dealer said.
By 0830 GMT the rand had recovered slightly to trade at 4.5825 on the dollar from 4.5685 at Wednesday's local close.
The central Reserve Bank was expected to enter the market to offer liquidity if the rand fell further to around the 4.59 level, widely expected to trigger a fall to a fresh low of 4.60.
"We haven't seen the bank yet, but he is likely to come in at the upper 4.58s. He doesn't want it to go to 4.60 and if it breaks 4.5890, it's likely to head there," another dealer said.

Long bonds also fell to their worst levels in two months in early trade, depressed by news the annual inflation rate last month rose to 8.4 percent, up from 7.5 percent in August, against expectations of an increase of 8.1 percent.
